entries.note: Preflight (inspectGame, above) reads the project's own declaration: the selected record is the one whose id matches gameId, or the first declared game when it is omitted; executable candidates resolve in order (absolute, root-relative with a Windows .exe fallback, bare name through the sidecar PATH), each declared requires file is stat'ed without symlink confinement so shared data can be linked in, as the qualification fixtures do, and a declared cwd must be an existing directory; nothing runs. embedded reserves a surface item and injects the macOS adapter (the qualified SDL interposition path); external spawns the plain PTY child so an SDL3/static application opens its own window and only its output is retained. Declared env is layered under the reservation and the adapter, and the reader already rejects RENGINE_/DYLD_/LD_ keys. Windows launch remains an explicit unsupported-integration error until the cooperative surface is wired and proven in that host.

anchor.snippet: const key = `${rootId}\0${config.id ?? ''}`; /* one launch per root AND declared game; see sidecar: launch-identity */

entries.note:
A launch is identified by root AND declared game id, not by root alone: contract 3 lets one project declare several games, and the owner's shape is that they run side by side (a flat target and a VR target at once). So concurrent requests coalesce per pair and a reuse only returns a running session whose game id matches. The preflight runs before the coalescing key exists because the key needs the resolved id, which also makes an unknown gameId a 404 rather than a silent default. An undeclared project fails before the reuse lookup so a game session started outside a declaration can never be handed back as "the project's game". The 2026-09-06 owner decision keeps that key when two dashboard actions name the same record with different argv: the declared id stays the single identity of a running game session (launch_game/game_preflight select by it, the snapshot carries it, the native tab binding and RENGINE_INITIAL_GAME resolve through it), so a differing launch is refused with both argv named rather than starting a second session under the same id or, worse, silently attaching and dropping the caller's arguments. The in-flight map therefore stores the argv beside the promise: an identical concurrent launch joins the flight, a differing one chains behind it and meets the same refusal instead of racing a second spawn.

The separator is written as the escape `\0`, not as the byte. It was typed as a literal NUL once, and a literal NUL makes grep, rg and every tool that sniffs for binary content treat this WHOLE FILE as binary and say nothing about it — a survey of which modules still imported a pair of shared rule modules came back clean while these lines imported both. Same string, searchable file; `suite-coverage.test.mjs` now asserts it.

The ONE difference between the two pane surfaces, and the reason cooperative is a separate enum value rather than a flag on embedded (spec 078, F77). Both reserve a Surfaces item and both are passed RENGINE_SURFACE_PORT/RENGINE_SURFACE_TOKEN; only embedded is also handed the adapter on DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES. If a game that connects for itself were ALSO injected, two producers would greet the same token on the same channel; Surfaces.accept keeps the first socket to arrive and destroys the second, and both clients reconnect after a close (the adapter has its own connect loop, the consumer's writer and reader threads retry), so the surviving producer is whichever wins a restart race -- on every reconnect, with no error reported anywhere. Keep this an equality test against 'embedded': widening it to streamsIntoPane() is exactly the edit that recreates the race, and orchestrator/tests/cooperative.test.mjs asserts against it by inspecting the environment this line composes (the child cannot report it -- macOS purges DYLD_* before a protected interpreter starts). The adapter and its macOS-only precondition live with the same equality test in inspectGame above, so a cooperative record is ready on every platform.
